task: Verify source-free multi-statement generic and nested private helper closure across independent consumer types
observation: The existing staged ABI-v10 harness ran a removed-source generic provider, and a reduced probe used one .mossi/.rlib to run independently compiled Int and String consumers (99 and hello). The apparent success came from generic_stmt fallback: inspect reported missing_typed_facts for fresh and both private helpers, while the interface had no private_semantic_dependencies or provenance records and only a hashless private helper name.
impact: Native output alone could falsely certify H3 even though checked open summaries, versioned body IR, and exact dependency/provenance hashes were absent from the source-free contract.

resolution.summary: The bounded H3 shape recognizer was removed. The source-free regression now verifies common occurrence-lowered checked-body records, strips legacy generic_stmt lines for the private chain, runs Int/String consumers without provider source, checks the checked-body projection trace, and rejects missing private-body records.

task: Emit versioned ABI-v10 checked body records from a live generic provider
observation: The first live direct-constructor provider failed before interface emission with SOURCE_FREE_CONTRACT_INVALID because the ABI-v10 container required every record payload to be UTF-8. Its versioned WireWriter payload was correctly byte-framed, but a checked-body length byte at or above 0x80 is not UTF-8 text.
impact: A valid rich semantic body could not enter the sealed .mossi even though the record codec and checker had canonical SHA-256 body facts.

resolution.summary: Record payloads remain exactly byte-framed and bounded; UTF-8 validation remains on record IDs and logical WireWriter string fields. The binary length round-trip and invalid logical-string negatives pass.

task: Prove that the exact H3 private identity helpers use common checked-body lowering
observation: The source-free H3 integration passed, but a focused in-memory provider assertion showed that identity_chain still used the migration fallback while private_identity used the common lowerer. A direct return-call operation had a result TypeRef but no copied argument TypeRefs; the checker retained ordered checked argument occurrences and a semantic call edge.
impact: Without checking the actual provider functions' provenance marker and decoded body, source-free execution could incorrectly count fallback bytes as generalized-lowering evidence. The exact-provider regression now checks both helper markers, canonical bytes/hash, expected body trees, source-free Int/String runs, poisoned legacy rows, and missing-body rejection.

resolution.summary: Common direct-return-call lowering links the checked result to the module-qualified selected callable, ordered argument occurrences, unique summary dependency, and exact semantic call edge. Receiver/argument ordinal mutations reject at positions 0 and 1. The exact provider regression verifies canonical H3 bodies and source-free Int/String consumers; the existing adversarial architect returned scoped GO with no P0/P1/P2 at d8b85055e44e8db4bb5607718fc0d00a3b5c2cca.
